To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the near-wall region is characterized by a very thin viscous sub-layer, a buffer layer and a fully turbulent layer.
the flow is very sensitive to the turbulence in the free stream and in the boundary layer.

the flow over the hill-shaped obstacle in the duct is highly three-dimensional, with a complex time-mean flow field and a rich spectrum of unsteadiness, including large-scale vortical structures and small-scale turbulence.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of the flow: (i) the time-resolved, large-eddy simulation (LES) of the flow; (ii) the development and application of statistical turbulence modelling; and (iii) the development of new, efficient and accurate numerical schemes.
the development, validation, and application of numerical methods and turbulence models for predicting turbulent flows over three-dimensional, curved surfaces.
the development of a robust and accurate numerical method for the simulation of such flows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of three-dimensional separated flows, the most accurate and reliable approach is to use a time-resolved DNS or LES.

the flow separation from curved, continuous surfaces is a complex, multi-scale phenomenon, and that it is very difficult to simulate accurately, even with the best numerical and modelling techniques available.
the flow over a hill is a very complex flow that can serve as a model for a wide variety of three-dimensional flows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simulation of such flows is now possible, and the results are of high enough accuracy that they can be used to test the performance of turbulence models.
the present simulation results are in very good agreement with the experimental data.
the present simulation is the most accurate and complete simulation of the flow separation from the hill obstacle in a duct.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the flow over a three dimensional obstacle in a duct can be predicted with high accuracy by the LES method using a high-order, low dissipation, low dispersion numerical scheme, such as the spectral vanishing viscosity (SVV) scheme, and a high-order, compact, low dissipation and low dispersion wall model, such as the wall model based on the SVV.
the flow separation process can be simulated with sufficient accuracy and resolution to capture the complex flow features and to resolve the near-wall flow.
the use of high-order numerical methods in conjunction with the proper choice of turbulence model can yield very accurate results.
